description: Universal rendering rules for tabletop miniature-style sculpt design visualizations - applicable to all character types

prop_visibility_modes.description: Defines how props interact with the character silhouette based on usage context

modes.presented: Prop held/displayed away from body; fully visible base-to-tip; clear negative space except at grip
modes.carried_attached: Prop worn/slung/holstered; overlap allowed at attachment zones; attachment method must be visible; item remains readable but does NOT require full base-to-tip visibility

generic_render_rules.description: Universal rendering rules applied to all prompts
rules: SINGLE SUBJECT ONLY: exactly one character/creature in the entire image. NO other figures, NO background characters, NO companions, NO additional people or animals. Only the main subject.
FIGURE-ONLY PRESENTATION: background blank/featureless (no scenery, terrain, set dressing, environmental objects, diorama elements, bases, pedestals, plinths, stands, or ground plane).

FRAMING (HARD CONSTRAINT): full-body figure entirely visible from head to feet; no cropping at ankles, knees, hips, shoulders, elbows, wrists, or head; all limbs fully inside frame; no cinematic crop, no hero crop, no portrait crop; generous negative space around entire figure.
View: three-quarter (3/4) sculpt view (~45° turntable rotation); NOT straight-on front view.

Camera: orthographic or neutral perspective (NOT cinematic); centered full-body framing (head-to-feet guaranteed); camera pulled back to include entire silhouette; no close-up, no medium shot, no waist-up framing; framing priority over facial detail.
Lighting: overhead key light with clear rim separation and subtle fill for edge definition. Use rim to define depth and emphasize form separation.

Design-intent anchor (CRITICAL): conceptual sculpt design visualization intended for tabletop-scale physical reproduction; illustrative art direction, not real-world documentation or evidence; do not reference existing brands or manufactured products.

Materials: uniform matte light-to-mid grey, unpainted miniature/resin model look used to communicate form only. Monochrome only — no painted colors, no dyed regions; no pure black or pure white. Even diffuse response for silhouette and plane readability; smooth surfaces with hard, crisp edges.

Rendering style (CRITICAL): HIGHLY STYLIZED ILLUSTRATION — graphic silhouettes, simplified planes, posterized value bands. Clean shapes and bold secondary forms; crisp plane breaks; hard, sharp edges. Coarse-to-medium texture scale; avoid fine microtexture, micro-noise, realistic skin pores, strand-level detail. Matte materials; no specular sparkle. Not photoreal.
Miniature readability (CRITICAL): prioritize medium-scale forms and flat/smooth planar surfaces with hard, crisp edges; avoid micro-engraving, filigree, and tiny surface noise.
Minimum feature size: avoid details smaller than ~0.5mm equivalent at tabletop scale; express detail as simple graphic cuts, chamfers, or broad grooves.

Texture: bold surface detail as graphic shapes with crisp edges and clean separation. Prefer smooth planar surfaces and hard-edged form transitions; prioritize form hierarchy: big shapes first, secondary forms next; texture scale stays coarse-to-medium (no ultra-fine noise).

No photographic artifacts: avoid lens effects (flare, bokeh), film grain, subsurface scattering, volumetric glow, chromatic aberration, and heavy depth-of-field blur. Keep illustrative clarity and graphic readability.

Fur/hair rendering (furred creatures only): bold clumps/tufts with deep grooves and clean separation between masses. NO individual hairs, NO micro-fuzz, NO flyaways, NO strand-level detail. Texture as graphic shapes, not noise.

Facial sculpt override (CRITICAL - 2D to 3D SAFE): Facial features expanded in width and height but intentionally shallow in depth. No deep cuts, cavities, or undercuts anywhere on the face. Brow ridge low-profile and blended—no shelf or overhang. Forehead, brow, cheeks, and nose formed from broad, flat primary planes with gentle transitions. Cheeks and mouth region treated as a single broad plane with minimal curvature—no hollowing or groove lines. Mouth indicated as a shallow notch rather than a recessed cavity. Teeth simplified into two shallow fang wedges with minimal depth. Eyes enlarged but shallow, with thick lids and no socket depth. All facial relief extremely shallow to prevent over-carving during 3D reconstruction. Facial detail resolution capped at ~0.5mm minimum feature size. Expression conveyed through silhouette, plane breaks, and jaw/eye angles rather than fine wrinkles. No skin pores, fine wrinkles, nasolabial folds, or subtle facial micro-texture.

Prop visibility modes (CRITICAL): Props follow one of two visibility modes depending on usage context. PRESENTED mode: prop held/displayed away from body; fully visible base-to-tip; clear negative space between prop and torso/limbs (except at grip/contact point). CARRIED_ATTACHED mode: prop worn, slung, holstered, sheathed, or strapped; overlap with body allowed ONLY at attachment/contact zones; attachment method (strap, sling, holster, sheath, belt loop) must be clearly visible; prop remains readable in silhouette but does NOT require full base-to-tip visibility.
Prop constraint (CRITICAL): do not add props unless explicitly specified. Only include items clearly named and described. Do not invent extra weapons, holsters, pouches, talismans, or implements.
Poses: must be readable from a single view without limb/object overlap. Held objects presented away from torso with clear negative space; avoid self-occluding silhouettes.

Value contrast (CRITICAL): depth expressed through greys. Darkest recesses as deep grey (not black); brightest planes as light grey (not pure white). Avoid flat lighting; emphasize overhead lighting for readable separation. CRITICAL: Dark values represent DEPTH ONLY (recesses, undercuts, shadows) NOT color. Surface color differences (e.g., eye pupils, dark fabric) rendered as mid-grey same as surrounding surfaces; only depth changes create value shifts.
generic_render_rules.prompt_snippet:
HIGHLY STYLIZED, NOT PHOTOREAL — conceptual sculpt design visualization for tabletop-scale reproduction.
Unpainted miniature look: uniform matte light-to-mid grey; smooth surfaces with hard, crisp edges; depth by greys (no color); no pure black or pure white. CRITICAL: dark values represent DEPTH ONLY (recesses, shadows) NOT color; surface color differences rendered as same mid-grey value; only depth/geometry changes create value shifts.
Miniature readability: medium-scale detail only; flat/smooth planar surfaces; hard, crisp edges; no filigree or micro-engraving; no tiny surface noise; minimum feature size about 0.5mm equivalent.

FACIAL SCULPT OVERRIDE (CRITICAL - 2D to 3D SAFE): Facial features expanded in width and height but intentionally shallow in depth. No deep cuts, cavities, or undercuts anywhere on the face. Brow ridge low-profile and blended—no shelf or overhang. Forehead, brow, cheeks, and nose formed from broad, flat primary planes with gentle transitions. Cheeks and mouth region treated as a single broad plane with minimal curvature—no hollowing or groove lines. Mouth indicated as a shallow notch rather than a recessed cavity. Teeth simplified into two shallow fang wedges with minimal depth. Eyes enlarged but shallow, with thick lids and no socket depth. All facial relief extremely shallow to prevent over-carving during 3D reconstruction.

FIGURE-ONLY PRESENTATION: single subject; background absent/blank; clear negative space; no scenery/base/stand/plinth/pedestal/ground plane; no invented props.
FRAMING (HARD CONSTRAINT): full body visible head-to-feet; no cropping at ankles/knees/hips/shoulders/elbows/wrists/head; limbs fully inside frame; no cinematic/hero/portrait crop; generous negative space around figure.
View: three-quarter (3/4) sculpt view (~45° turntable rotation); NOT straight-on front view.

Camera: orthographic or neutral perspective (not cinematic); centered full-body framing (head-to-feet guaranteed); camera pulled back to include entire silhouette; no close-up, no medium shot, no waist-up framing; framing priority over facial detail.
Lighting: overhead key + rim separation; neutral illumination emphasizing plane breaks and silhouette readability.
Style: graphic silhouettes, posterized value bands, simplified planes, clean plane transitions; smooth planar surfaces; hard, sharp edges; coarse-to-medium textures; matte surfaces; no lens/film effects.
